newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes punch higher in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes punch higher in quiet session.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices narrowed grade differential discounts against a weakening outright benchmark in featureless Friday afternoon action.
Deals were recorded for most grades, but the volume levels and frequency of trades failed to excite market participants.
"People are covering their ratable barrel needs," said one trader.

May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing retreated from earlier gains to losses of around 5 cents, putting the benchmark WTI at $19.45-55 a barrel, while May/June WTI narrowed to around 7 cts from 10-11 cts in the morning.
Outright prices have fallen back on pressure from a heating oil sell-off, temporarily brushing aside concerns over a growing diplomatic feud between Iran and the European Union.

Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James has traded at 29 and 30 cts under WTI/Cushing, with no fresh deals seen. Other afternoon trades were seen for West Texas Sour/Midland at discounts of $2.26, $2.27 and $2.29 to the marker.
Firmer Brent prices, along with other North Sea physical barrels, has made domestic grades more attractive. In recent weeks, sweet crudes have been hurt by cheap foreign crudes.
Traders said even though prices for sweet and sour grades have improved, there remains plenty of crude available from many locales.
